questions_and_answers.question_text: How is the adjectival verb duō used in No. 7?
Which other word may be used in the same way?
Write the Chinese for "Eat a little more."
Write the Chinese for "He stayed two days longer."
What is the literal meaning of Wǒ shǎo mǎile yìzhāng piào?
Write the Chinese for "One must not drink too much coffee."
Write the Chinese for "He says he wants to eat less."

answers.answer_text: Tā shuō tā yào shǎo chī.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "I hope that in the future we will have an opportunity to meet more."

answers.answer_text: Xīwàng yǐhòu yǒu jīhui duō jiànmiàn.

articles.text:
7. B: Nǎli, nǎli.                    Not at all, not at all.
   B: Xīwàng yǐhòu yǒu jīhui duō     I hope that in the future we will
      jiànmiàn.                       have an opportunity to meet more.

Note on No. 7

The adjectival verb duō, "to be much," "to be many," is used in No. 7 as an adverb meaning "much," "more." Shǎo may be used in the same way.

Kāfēi bù néng duō hē.            One must not drink too much coffee.
Nǐ duō chī diǎnr ba.             Eat a little more.
Tā duō zhùle liǎngtiān.          He stayed two days longer.
Wǒ shǎo mǎile yìzhāng piào.      I bought one ticket too few. (more
                                 literally, "I underbought by one
                                 ticket.")
Tā shuō tā yào shǎo chī.         He says he wants to eat less (cut
                                 down on eating).
